name: Movement Continuity B-Roll
source_tutorial: knowledge/research/transcripts/what not to do in editing.txt
use_when: Several B-roll shots need to feel connected as one journey, city entrance, or exploration sequence.
Rapid shot changes make the viewer feel thrown around the frame.
The sequence uses walking, drone, vehicle, or camera movement shots.
Camera movement direction can express story meaning, such as pulling viewers out of a fantasy or inviting them into a world.
avoid_when: The intended emotion is chaos, rupture, or disorientation.
Flipping or reordering motion would misrepresent geography, signs, text, or truthful direction.
The sequence is built around contrast rather than flow.

timeline_pattern.direction_rule: Keep camera or subject motion direction consistent across adjacent flow shots.
timeline_pattern.story_direction_rule: Tracking back can create distance, reveal scale, or pull the viewer out; tracking forward can invite the viewer into a world or idea.
timeline_pattern.cadence_rule: Let each shot resolve enough for the viewer to scan the focal point.
timeline_pattern.entering_place_rule: Use one strong establishing shot, then slower focal movement shots to let the viewer enter the location.
timeline_pattern.exception_rule: A striking image can break movement cohesion when a new beat or sound cue makes the break feel intentional.

motion.rule: Match pan, walk, drone, vehicle, or subject direction unless a motivated contrast is needed.

keyframe_values.minimum_scan_hold: For documentary B-roll, start around 1.5-3 seconds per meaningful shot; go longer for dense destruction, maps, or signs.
keyframe_values.soft_transition: Use a short dissolve or J-cut when entering a calmer location; avoid trendy wipes for mature documentary tone.
keyframe_values.direction_fix: Horizontal flip only when no text/geography/truth issue is introduced.
keyframe_values.break_beat: When breaking a movement run, add a clear sound cue or 1-2 second pause beat so the new image reads as deliberate.

sound.rule: Use ambience or J-cuts to smooth entry into a location sequence; use a distinct sound beat when breaking movement cohesion for story effect.

captions.rule: Keep captions stable during movement sequences so they do not add another competing motion path.

color.rule: Match exposure and contrast across movement shots so continuity feels intentional.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use hflip cautiously for direction matching; inspect frames for reversed text or false geography. Build contact sheets to compare motion direction.
implementation.remotion: Add direction metadata to B-roll clips and assemble same-direction runs before introducing contrast or a marked movement-break beat.
implementation.blender: Use camera moves that continue the same screen direction across cuts when building map or location animation.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Choose shots with matching movement direction; avoid stacking fast random travel clips.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use clip labels for left-to-right, right-to-left, push-in, pull-out, and static shots; assemble movement strings by label.

common_mistakes: Cutting left-to-right into right-to-left movement without purpose.
Using too many quick drone shots instead of one strong establishing shot.
Making the viewer search for a focal point while the shot is already gone.
Using screen wipes where movement continuity would be cleaner.
Breaking a track-in or track-out run without adding a story reason, pause, or sound cue.
qc: Do adjacent flow shots move in compatible directions?
Does each shot have enough hold time to scan the focal point?
Would any flipped shot reverse text, maps, traffic, or truthful geography?
Does the location entrance feel like arrival rather than random coverage?
If movement direction changes, is the break motivated by story, image strength, or a sound beat?
